article.title: Ubiquitous
article.description: Meaning: present, appearing, or found everywhere. Pronunciation: yoo-BIK-wi-tuhs. Example: 'Smartphones have become ubiquitous in modern life.' Register: formal/academic, common in IELTS Writing Task 2 essays about technology or globalization.
article.content: Meaning: present, appearing, or found everywhere. Pronunciation: yoo-BIK-wi-tuhs. Example: 'Smartphones have become ubiquitous in modern life.' Register: formal/academic, common in IELTS Writing Task 2 essays about technology or globalization.

generated.caption:
Ever feel like certain things are just *everywhere* these days? That's when you can use **ubiquitous**! (yoo-BIK-wi-tuhs)

It means something is present, appearing, or found everywhere. This formal word is perfect for IELTS essays.

For example: 'Smartphones have become ubiquitous in modern life.'

Save this word to boost your vocabulary and follow @TheEnglishVault for daily English tips!
generated.script: Ye difficult sa word 'Ubiquitous' sunke aap bhi confuse ho jaate ho na? Toh dekho, 'Ubiquitous' ka matlab hai koi aisi cheez jo har jagah present ho, matlab sab jagah dikhti ho. Iska pronunciation hai 'yoo-BIK-wi-tuhs'. Yeh ek thoda formal word hai, often IELTS jaise exams mein kaam aata hai. For example, 'Smartphones have become ubiquitous in modern life'. Toh basically, agar koi cheez literally everywhere hai, toh aap use 'ubiquitous' bol sakte ho. Simple, right? Comment mein batao aapke life mein kya cheez 'ubiquitous' hai! slides.body: The adjective 'ubiquitous', pronounced yoo-BIK-wi-tuhs, describes something that is present, appearing, or found everywhere. It's a powerful word to convey widespread presence. For example, 'Smartphones have become ubiquitous in modern life' clearly illustrates how common these devices are. This is a formal and academic term, highly useful in essays for exams like IELTS Writing Task 2, especially when discussing topics like technology or globalization.
